article_title: The Effect of Written Corrective Feedback on Grammatical Accuracy of EFL Students: An Improvement over Previous Unfocused Designs
citation: Mobin Khanlarzadeh, Majid Nemati. (2016). The effect of written corrective feedback on grammatical accuracy of EFL students: An improvement over previous unfocused designs. Iranian Journal of Language Teaching Research 4(2). https://www.urmia.ac.ir/ijltr
title: Treat WCF as one option among several, with teachers making professional decisions based on context
description: The article recommends against total abandonment of written corrective feedback while rejecting the view that it must always be provided. It holds that "provision of WCF must be regarded as only one of the options teachers have for improving learners' grammatical accuracy," and that teachers should weigh their experience with similar students, student numbers, learners' age and proficiency, course purpose, available time, and other classroom limitations when deciding.
requirements: Teachers base the decision on previous experience with similar students, class size, learner age and proficiency level, course purpose, available time, and other classroom limitations
constraints: The study's evidence covers elementary EFL learners revising without follow-up teacher-student interaction
examples: The study found WCF helped revision-time error reduction but did not significantly affect accuracy on a new writing task, grounding the recommendation that WCF is one option rather than an obligatory practice.
key_sources: Mobin Khanlarzadeh, Majid Nemati. (2016). The effect of written corrective feedback on grammatical accuracy of EFL students: An improvement over previous unfocused designs. Iranian Journal of Language Teaching Research 4(2). https://www.urmia.ac.ir/ijltr

article_title: Beliefs, practices, and awareness of written corrective feedback among EFL teachers: a mixed-methods study.
citation: Mostafavi Marzieh, Shokrpour Nasrin, Afraz Shahram. (2025). Beliefs, practices, and awareness of written corrective feedback among EFL teachers: a mixed-methods study. BMC Psychology. https://doi.org/10.1186/s40359-025-03861-z
title: Model of teacher WCF awareness and practice as mediation between cognition and context
description: Derived from the interview themes and quantitative findings (Fig. 1), the model represents teachers' awareness and beliefs—formed mainly by experience and a holistic view of writing—as their cognitions, while actual practices result from dynamic mediation between these cognitions and contextual factors. The article states practices are "a product of the dynamic negotiation, or mediation, between these cognitions and powerful contextual factors such as time constraints, student proficiency levels, and institutional demands". This explains why areas less affected by constraints, like direct/selective preference, show stronger alignment.
requirements: Teacher awareness and beliefs formed predominantly by experience and a holistic view of writing as the cognitive input
constraints: Derived from a specific Iranian EFL university teacher population; contextual factors named are time constraints, student proficiency levels, and institutional demands
target_learning_goals: Understanding and improving written corrective feedback practice and teacher awareness
examples: The model visually represents mediation explaining belief-practice discrepancies in comprehensive feedback and error codes while gender-neutral evaluation showed stronger alignment
key_sources: Mostafavi Marzieh, Shokrpour Nasrin, Afraz Shahram. (2025). Beliefs, practices, and awareness of written corrective feedback among EFL teachers: a mixed-methods study. BMC Psychology. https://doi.org/10.1186/s40359-025-03861-z

article_title: Reciprocal Predictions Between Reading Achievement and Cognitive Flexibility Development in Children and the Mediating Roles of the Left Middle Frontal Gyrus.
citation: Ma, L., Wang, Y., Wang, J., et al. (2025). Reciprocal Predictions Between Reading Achievement and Cognitive Flexibility Development in Children and the Mediating Roles of the Left Middle Frontal Gyrus. Human Brain Mapping. https://doi.org/10.1002/hbm.70309
title: New continuous cognitive flexibility index combining WCST switches and correct responses
description: The authors developed a new cognitive flexibility index from the Wisconsin Card Sorting Task, combining the number of switches and correct responses into a continuous variable. They note that perseverative errors "may not capture subtle differences between individuals" and that a prior sensitivity index was "unable to account for individual differences in categorical data". The new index had a Cronbach's α of 0.986 and was designed to provide "a more accurate reflection of individual differences".
requirements: WCST administration with computer feedback and grouping of children by number of switches to compute within-group correct-response maxima and minima
constraints: Developed and validated within this study's cohort of Chinese school-aged children
key_sources: Ma, L., Wang, Y., Wang, J., et al. (2025). Reciprocal Predictions Between Reading Achievement and Cognitive Flexibility Development in Children and the Mediating Roles of the Left Middle Frontal Gyrus. Human Brain Mapping. https://doi.org/10.1002/hbm.70309
